assumptions: Preserve v2 two-sided97.5% marginal scientific intervals. The one-sided guardrail tail is .0125, not the reviewer approximate .025 backsolve.
Shared-episode variance is divided by M, never by N*M. Pilot residual variance is separately divided by N*M.
Pilot SD is max of corrected paired tracking and corrected paired post-collision seed SD; signed unconstrained components are retained.
Predeclared near-boundary radius .005 moves SD>=.025 to recomputation and SD>=.045 to STOP. Nominal .03/.05 boundaries remain documented.
Five-pair Gaussian crossed-ANOVA variance-component confidence interval is conservative within that model, not distribution-free coverage.
Full practical-point-target classifications cannot have80% power at exact SESOI under the symmetric working model; detection powers do not claim otherwise.
Scientific seed count is chosen using Frechet lower bound >.8 for collision detection AND tracking guardrail. No joint probability product.
Joint bounds use directional collision superiority, excluding the tiny opposite-direction rejection tail; the v2 two-sided detection power is also saved separately.
Methodological variance is not identified by CL-minus-OL pilot; floor max(.03, pilot gate SD) is a planning transfer assumption only. Classic/BPTT differences remain unmeasured.
The pilot uses fixed defaults before later validation-based hyperparameter selection. Its variability need not transfer to selected full-study configurations.
Measured shared-episode/residual components may raise counts even when seed SD is small; original episode assumptions are floors, not overwritten by favorable pilot noise.
Scientific failure penalties remain in the variance estimate; low variance does not establish task learning. Incomplete infrastructure outcomes cannot pass.
No graph-SD pilot is required or run for R1. R2 remains deferred.
